claims.statement: Mechanism behind claims 4/5's asymmetry: the affine marks of E6, read directly off the exactly-computed highest root (1,2,2,3,2,1), are (affine node 1; nodes 1-6: 1,2,2,3,2,1) — all <= 3. This explains, not merely restates, why all 9 order-5 rows carry u(1)-count >= 1 while orders 2 and 3 each contain exactly one center-0 row.

sel.fail_witnesses:
MB12 non-vacuity, exhibited concretely at three separate levels (each level was checked in BOTH directions, not just the direction that supports the headline):

(1) The su(3)-singlet test itself is NOT a tautology that always returns nonzero -- WITNESS: B932's own conformal chain (the S-subalgebra su(3)+su(2)+su(2), center 0, index (2,3,1)) gives EXACTLY 0 (results.json: color_singlet_states=0). The test is a real two-outcome predicate on su(3) embeddings in general.

(2) Yet restricted to the domain B932's own T1+T2 define as 'reachable' (index-1, root-generated su(3)'s), the test is EXHAUSTIVELY constant at 9 -- not sampled: all 120 distinct A2 subsystems of E6, zero exceptions. This is the sharp, falsifiable finding: had even ONE of the 120 given a different count (0, or any value other than 9), the 'forced' claim would have failed instantly at that witness. It did not fail. This IS the bite: a real dichotomy (9 vs 0) cutting exactly along the index-1/index-2 line B932's T2 already drew, now shown quantitatively and exhaustively rather than just qualitatively for one pair of candidates.

(3) The domain-membership question (does a row even HAVE an su(3) factor) is genuinely two-sided and non-vacuous: 2 of 9 row-TYPES do (su(3)+su(2)+su(2)+u(1)^2, su(3)+su(3)+su(2)+u(1)), 7 do not -- and by raw point-count the split is 5760 vs 9864 of 15624 (80/217 vs 137/217 exactly), a real, non-degenerate partition, not '1 row' or '8 rows'. A vacuous result would have looked like EVERY row carrying an su(3) factor (making 'is there a subject' trivially always-yes) or NO row carrying one (making B932's criterion trivially inapplicable to the whole menu); neither happened.

(4) The EXTENSION (full-semisimple-singlet) criterion is independently non-vacuous with a real spread across the 9 rows (0,0,0,1,1,1,2,3,5 -- three exact zeros, six positive values up to 5), AND it disagrees with the literal criterion on su(3)+su(3)+su(2)+u(1) (literal: SPEAKS via 9-and-9; extension: SILENT via 0) -- proof that 'generalize B932's criterion to rows without su(3)' is a real, consequential, not-yet-adjudicated design choice rather than a notational triviality. A vacuous extension would have agreed with the literal test everywhere it overlapped, or would itself have been constant across all 9 rows; neither happened.

Net: LEG1, on its native domain (rows/subalgebras that actually have an su(3)), kills NOTHING -- 120/120 regular su(3)'s speak, 0/120 are silent, and both Wilson-menu rows that qualify speak. LEG2 (T1+T2) kills nothing among the 9 either, but for a different, structural reason: it cannot, by the menu's own construction (every row already IS the kind of object T1+T2 describe). The real 'kill' in this whole exercise happened once, already, inside B932 itself, against the ONE candidate (the conformal chain) that was never a Wilson-menu row to begin with and never could be.
